questions.prompt: Explain how buildgum builds a checkout quote from the cart, and why the cart does not own prices.

keyPoints.text: The cart only stores product ids and quantities, not prices.
keyPoints.quote: The cart stores product identifiers and quantities. It does not own prices.

keyPoints.text: Each item is resolved against the accepted catalog; unavailable products and duplicate lines are rejected.
keyPoints.quote: resolves each item against the accepted catalog, rejects unavailable products and duplicate lines

keyPoints.text: Quantities must be between one and ninety-nine.
keyPoints.quote: validates quantities from one through ninety-nine

keyPoints.text: Lines are sorted by id so cart order cannot change the fingerprint.
keyPoints.quote: It sorts lines by identifier so equivalent cart ordering does not change the fingerprint.

keyPoints.text: The quote carries computed amounts plus the accepted product and discount versions.
keyPoints.quote: The quote contains computed amounts and accepted product and discount versions.

keyPoints.text: That lets the reducer detect a changed quote later.
keyPoints.quote: The reducer can therefore detect a changed quote later.

questions.prompt: Walk through freezing an attempt and replaying it: what is captured, when, and what does replay return?

keyPoints.text: The first checkout request creates the order id, request key, normalized buyer, timestamp and quote.
keyPoints.quote: the UI creates an order ID, request key, normalized buyer address, timestamp, and quote

keyPoints.text: Inputs are disabled while the attempt is unresolved.
keyPoints.quote: Inputs become disabled while the attempt remains unresolved.

keyPoints.text: Retry resends the same command instead of rebuilding it.
keyPoints.quote: Retry sends the same command instead of rebuilding it from possibly changed fields.

keyPoints.text: A retry keeps the original purchase time.
keyPoints.quote: A retry does not invent a newer purchase time.

keyPoints.text: Inside the lock, replay looks for a receipt with the same request key and returns the workspace when the fingerprint matches.
keyPoints.quote: If the fingerprint matches, the existing workspace is returned immediately.

keyPoints.text: This works even with an old baseline because nothing new is applied.
keyPoints.quote: This can succeed even when the caller's baseline is old

questions.prompt: Explain the lost-acknowledgement problem and the remaining gap between a local receipt and a real payment.

keyPoints.text: React accepts the new snapshot only after setItem returns.
keyPoints.quote: React accepts that snapshot only after `setItem` returns successfully.

keyPoints.text: An exception after the real write is a lost acknowledgement; the UI keeps the attempt.
keyPoints.quote: An exception after the actual write represents a lost acknowledgement.

keyPoints.text: Retrying finds the receipt already stored, so there is still exactly one.
keyPoints.quote: Retrying finds the receipt already in storage, so the count remains one.

keyPoints.text: The client cannot distinguish rejection from a lost acknowledgement, so retries must be safe in both cases.
keyPoints.quote: the client cannot tell "rejected" from "acknowledgement lost" by itself, so the retry must be safe under both

keyPoints.text: A new key after a lost acknowledgement would create a second order.
keyPoints.quote: A retry with a *new* key after a lost acknowledgement creates a second order

keyPoints.text: The flow is a simulated receipt: no money, inventory, licences, taxes or email.
keyPoints.quote: It does not authorize money, reserve inventory, issue licenses, calculate taxes, or send email.

keyPoints.text: Real payment needs server authorization, provider idempotency, durable attempts and reconciliation.
keyPoints.quote: Payment integration needs server authorization, provider idempotency, durable attempts, reconciliation
